name: Hand painted Silk Hankies - Silk spinning / knitting / felting fiber, 13 g - Terra 1
description: Use these silk hankies for spinning, knitting directly, nuno felting, wet or needle felting, or in paper making, textile collage, or carding into batts. This silk hankie or mawata is shades of green.Each hankie is a silk cocoon that is stretched over a square frame to form a thin irregular layer. Centers are gossamer, edges are thicker. To knit directly without spinning, separate one hankie and push your fingers through the middle of the hankie. Start stretching the resulting hole wider and wider. You can pull the hankie out to worsted or even DK diameter by "drafting" all around the loop to the desired thickness. It will stretch easier if your hands are a foot apart or more. Break the silk when you have make your loop as large as you want. Now you are ready to knit your first hankie from one end of your yarn. You can also spin from your drafted fiber and make quite a fine yarn. Have fun! Hankies with the same name that are numbered sequentially have been dyed together, and are a matched set, although they may differ slightly in weight and appearance.13 g, 0.5 oz.All hankies are dyed with professional acid dyes and set with steam, in a non-smoking, pet friendly environment.
